sources.note: Lists Yimas-Iatmul Pidgin among four Glottolog-coded Yimas pidgins with no source; for the LEXIFIER Yimas it reports (after Foley 1991) initial primary stress with secondary on the third syllable and epenthetic-vowel exceptions -- second-hand and about Yimas proper, not the pidgin.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2013. Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin (survey chapter 69). In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds.), The Survey of Pidgin and Creole Languages, vol. III; APiCS Online, https://apics-online.info/surveys/69 (CC-BY 4.0).
sources.note: Describes the SISTER pidgin Yimas-Arafundi (yima1244), not Yimas-Iatmul. Sec. 4 Phonology gives 4 vowels (with /ə/ largely epenthetic, as in Yimas) and 15-16 consonants; nothing at all on stress or accent. Sec. 2 says Yimas-Arafundi is 'one of a family of Yimas-based pidgins... There are at least three others (Williams 2000)'; names the Alamblak and Karawari partners; Iatmul is not mentioned.
